admission.justification: Three input rules were weighed and D46 chose one; every later family judgment and refusal text must obey the chosen rule.

alternatives.option: Require the curator-authored effect from the existing vocabulary on every new or edited changed family row; the writer stores exactly it and derives none.
alternatives.reason: D46 settles the input rule, and the writer must not judge whether an authored effect is right: code records identities while the curator judges meaning.

alternatives.option: Leave the effect optional on new changed rows.
alternatives.reason: With nothing stored, the effect display has nothing to show; the omission that motivated D46 persists.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The effect display stops needing a stored effect for a changed row.

alternatives.option: Let the writer derive the label from the guarantee wording, reason, disposition, counts, members or a member effect.
alternatives.reason: Derivation invents a curator judgment the curator never made; the packet forbids every one of these sources.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The effect becomes computable from record deltas without inventing a judgment.

consequences: Changed family rows without a valid authored effect are refused naming row and family.
Effects on rerouted, assigned, no_impact and retired rows are refused naming row and field.
Curators following older instruction text are refused with the remedy until rule 7 lands.
context: D46 requires the effect label on new and edited changed family rows, decided 2026-10-04; the writer accepted a hand-off effect and then dropped it, so the reviewer could not show the effect of a family's meaning change.
